subject: sociology

moments.title: The Communist Manifesto
moments.body: Written in London on the eve of Europe's 1848 revolutions, the pamphlet sketches a theory of history as class struggle.
moments.takeaway: Sociological theory and revolutionary politics emerge intertwined.

moments.title: Capital, volume one
moments.body:
Marx analyses commodity exchange, surplus value and the accumulation of capital using British factory data.

Volumes two and three are published posthumously by Engels.
moments.takeaway: Long-form economic analysis grounded Marx's broader sociological framework.

moments.title: Piketty's Capital in the Twenty-First Century
moments.body: Piketty's long-run tax data reopen debates about capital accumulation and inequality, arguing that returns on capital tend to outpace economic growth.
moments.takeaway: Empirical revival of classical questions can reshape contemporary political debate.

now.title: Class analysis today
now.body: Modern stratification research uses occupational, cultural and wealth measures (e.g. Savage et al.'s 2013 'Great British Class Survey'). Wealth taxation is debated in OECD countries.
now.open_questions: How should new asset categories (housing, pensions, digital) be incorporated into class measures? Does globalisation alter class formation?

reflection: Marx's predictions about industrial proletariat formation took unexpected paths in different national contexts.
